label: Gearbox
description: Enclosed industrial speed-reducer gearbox with oil lubrication.
general_safety: Isolate and lock out the drive and secure the load against movement before opening any gearbox cover.
Gearbox oil can be hot: let it cool or wear heat-resistant gloves and eye protection when draining or sampling.
Vent pressure through the breather before removing fill or drain plugs.
general_inspection: Check the oil level, colour and smell, and take an oil sample if possible.
Check visually for leaks at seals, covers and the breather.
Compare casing temperature and noise with a known-good reading for this gearbox.

faults.name: Gear tooth wear or damage
faults.reasoning: Worn, pitted or chipped gear teeth produce whining or grinding noise and raised vibration, often with metal particles in the oil.

triggers.symptom: Whining or grinding noise from the gears
Notes mention gear damage, metal particles or backlash

inspection_steps: Inspect the oil and magnetic drain plug for metal particles or flakes.
Look through the inspection cover for pitting, scuffing or chipped teeth.
Check backlash against the manufacturer's limit.
Take vibration readings if a meter is available and compare over time.
maintenance_actions: Change the oil and flush the gearbox if contamination is found.
Replace damaged gears or the gear set in matched pairs.
Check alignment and loading to find what caused the wear.
safety: Lock out the drive and block the output shaft before opening the cover.
Wear gloves when handling gears; broken teeth can be sharp.

faults.name: Lubrication problem (low, degraded or wrong oil)
faults.reasoning: Too little, overfilled, degraded or wrong-grade oil raises friction and churning heat, which shows up as high temperature and then noise and wear.

triggers.symptom: High oil or casing temperature (85 °C or more)
Oil loss can lower the oil level
Notes mention oil level, condition or grade

inspection_steps: Check the oil level at the sight glass or dipstick and look for overfilling.
Check the oil colour, smell, foaming and water contamination.
Confirm the oil grade and viscosity match the manufacturer's specification.
Check the breather and cooling (fan, cooler, fins) for blockage.
maintenance_actions: Top up or drain to the correct level with the specified oil.
Change degraded oil and the filter, and clear the breather.
Clean cooling surfaces and check ambient temperature.
safety: Let hot oil cool before draining or sampling.
Dispose of used oil according to site rules and clean spills immediately.

faults.name: Bearing wear
faults.reasoning: Worn gearbox bearings cause rumbling or grinding noise, rising vibration and heat at the shaft ends.

triggers.symptom: High temperature near the bearing housings

inspection_steps: Compare housing temperature at the input and output shaft bearings.
Listen with a stethoscope near each bearing housing.
Check shaft end float and free rotation by hand, with the gearbox locked out.
Check the oil for bearing metal.
maintenance_actions: Replace worn bearings and check shaft and housing fits.
Change the oil and clean the gearbox after the repair.
Check alignment and belt or chain loads on the shafts.
safety: Lock out the drive before touching shafts or couplings.
Support heavy components with proper lifting equipment when removing covers.

faults.name: Shaft misalignment / coupling problem
faults.reasoning: Misalignment between the gearbox and motor or driven shaft loads the bearings and seals and produces high vibration, often with knocking noise.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention alignment, coupling or shaft problems

inspection_steps: Check input and output shaft alignment with a dial gauge or laser tool.
Inspect the coupling for wear, backlash or damaged elements.
Check for soft foot and loose mounting bolts.
Check for oil leakage at the shaft seals, which misalignment accelerates.
maintenance_actions: Re-align the gearbox within the coupling tolerance.
Correct the base or shimming if it is uneven.
safety: Lock out the drive and secure the load before touching the coupling.

faults.name: Oil leak / seal failure
faults.reasoning: Worn shaft seals, loose covers or a blocked breather let oil escape, which can lower the oil level and lead to overheating and wear.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention oil leakage, seals or the breather
Raised temperature, possibly from low oil

inspection_steps: Find the source: input or output shaft seal, cover joint, drain plug or breather.
Check the oil level and top up temporarily if safe to do so.
Check that the breather is clear; a blocked breather raises internal pressure.
Check shaft surfaces under the seals for grooves or wear.
maintenance_actions: Replace the leaking seal and check the shaft surface.
Re-seal cover joints and tighten bolts evenly.
Clear or replace the breather and restore the correct oil level.
safety: Clean oil off floors and walkways promptly to avoid slips.
Lock out the drive before working near the shaft seals.

faults.name: Overload / shock loading
faults.reasoning: Loads above the gearbox rating, or repeated shocks from jams and hard starts, overheat the oil and stress the gears, bearings and shafts.

triggers.symptom: Knocking under load, typical of shock loading
Notes mention overload, jams or shock loads

inspection_steps: Compare the actual load or motor current with the gearbox rating and service factor.
Check the driven machine for jams, binding or intermittent heavy loads.
Check the starting method and the number of starts per hour.
Inspect couplings, keys and shafts for signs of shock damage.
maintenance_actions: Reduce the load or fix the process cause of the shocks.
Fit or adjust a torque limiter or soft starter where appropriate.
Review gearbox sizing if the real duty is above its rating.
safety: Lock out the drive and release stored energy in the driven machine before clearing a jam.
Do not restart repeatedly after a trip; investigate first.
